Resolution Minerals eyes larger Golden Gate gold play
articles.description: Resolution Minerals Ltd US operations chief executive Craig Lindsay talked with Proactive about the latest drilling results from the company’s 100%-owned Horse Heaven Project in Idaho, where Golden Gate North has developed into a broad gold-mineralised system extending for at least 500 metres. Lindsay said the latest results came from the company’s 42-hole, approximately 12,000-metre drilling campaign across Golden Gate North and Golden Gate South. The first holes reported from Golden Gate North included broad mineralised intervals of 324 metres at 0.49 g/t gold and 322 metres at 0.37 g/t gold, with mineralisation extending from surface to the bottom of the holes. The drilling has expanded Golden Gate North to around 500 metres in length and about 200 metres in width. Lindsay said the wider opportunity was the potential for Golden Gate North and Golden Gate South, around two kilometres apart, to form part of one much larger mineralised system. Golden Gate South has already returned a broad intersection of around 305 metres at 0.64 g/t gold, while Lindsay said drilling across the broader Golden Gate fault zone was continuing to demonstrate continuity and locally higher-grade gold. Resolution Minerals has so far reported results from only the first nine holes of the 2026 campaign, leaving results from more than 30 additional holes still to come. Lindsay also highlighted upcoming tungsten results from Golden Gate, which could add another dimension to the project alongside gold and antimony. Looking ahead to 2027, the company expects investors to see a maiden mineral resource estimate covering Golden Gate North and South. Resolution Minerals is also progressing permitting for further drilling at Golden Gate and Antimony Ridge. Visit Proactive’s YouTube channel for more interviews and market updates. articles.title: Carnavale Resources' Kookynie Gold Project BFS delivers A$104M pre tax cash flow
articles.description: Carnavale Resources Ltd managing director Humphrey Hale talked with Proactive about the bankable feasibility study (BFS) for the initial open-pit development of the Kookynie Gold Project in Western Australia. The study outlines A$104 million in pre-tax free cash flow over an 18-month mine life, with the development centred on the high-grade Swiftsure and Tiptoe open pits. Hale described the BFS as an important milestone for a deposit Carnavale discovered and has continued to advance through drilling and technical studies. The initial development is based on contract mining and third-party processing rather than the construction of a standalone plant. Hale said this approach allows Carnavale to reduce its capital requirements, with peak funding estimated at around A$24 million, while taking advantage of established processing infrastructure in the Goldfields. Swiftsure is the larger of the two starter pits and contains ore grading around 5.8 grams per tonne gold, while Tiptoe averages around 2.7 grams per tonne. Carnavale is now focused on securing an ore purchase agreement or toll treatment arrangement to establish the processing route and underpin project funding. The company is targeting the second half of 2027 for the start of open-pit production, subject to approvals, funding and a final investment decision. articles.title: Matrix Critical Minerals targets IPO as Narraburra rare earths project advances
articles.description: Matrix Critical Minerals Limited executive chairman Chris Gibbs spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the company’s planned IPO, the potential of its Narraburra Rare Earths Project in New South Wales, and efforts to engage strategic partners and offtake customers. Matrix is being spun out of Orbit Resources to unlock value from Narraburra, which had been put on hold while its parent focused on the Lewis Ponds gold and silver project. Gibbs said changing market conditions and Chinese export controls had renewed interest in alternative rare earth supplies. He highlighted Narraburra’s heavy rare earth content, including yttrium, dysprosium and terbium. Metallurgical testing with the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO) has produced a mixed rare earth carbonate containing 18.7% yttrium. Two batches have been produced, with further test work planned to refine product specifications and meet customer requirements. Gibbs also discussed meetings with potential offtake partners and the role of early customer engagement in building strategic relationships. The company plans further demonstration plant testing alongside project studies. Gibbs outlined Narraburra’s infrastructure advantages, including sealed-road access, nearby mining communities, an established workforce and power infrastructure. The IPO offer is open, with the company aiming to list before the end of 2026. Watch the full interview for more on the offer, Narraburra’s development plans and the next steps towards potential commercial partnerships.
